**Finding submitted: `missing` (WARRANTY) — confidence 0.86**

**What I found.** Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only the mutual corporate boilerplate — organization, authority, enforceability, no conflict (p0056–p0057) — plus an HDI acknowledgement about the Globix Agreement (p0058). Sweeping the rest of the document turned up no express performance warranty from HDI on the work it is actually paid to do (design, development, implementation, hosting, maintenance), no conformance period, no legal-compliance or malicious-code warranty, and no remedy.

**Direction check.** Section 1.6 (Site operational in 60 days, Company termination right at 70 days) and Section 5.2 (Company acceptance and approval in writing) are delivery and approval mechanics that benefit us, not warranties — I did not treat them as satisfying the rule, and did not flag them.

**Classification.** There is no disclaimer clause anywhere, so this is not walk-away "AS IS" territory. But the total absence of an express performance warranty falls below even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), and the rule's detection guidance directs that a missing express warranty be cured by insertion.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New Section 9(c) inserted after p0058 at the preferred position: workmanlike performance consistent with industry standards; 90-day conformance of the Site and deliverables, keyed to the existing Section 5.2 acceptance mechanic; compliance with applicable law; no virus or malicious code; with a re-performance / repair-or-replace / refund-of-fees remedy at HDI's option. I anchored the conformance trigger to Section 5.2 rather than inventing a new acceptance concept, and defined "Services" inline since the term is used in Section 8.1 but never formally defined.
